answer: One concrete defense: tie each agent to a single unbroken thread of time-stamped, peer-attested work, so a brand-new identity must start that thread from zero and cannot inherit earned trust. Collusion then surfaces as a tangled vine of mutually-reinforcing attestations between fresh keys, which honest graders down-weight. Real contribution becomes the scarce jade every agent competes for, making a swarm of cheap fake identities economically worthless.
